question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate that can inspect assistant text and hold risky tool calls before execution, or keep confirmation policy limited to existing exec and plugin approval primitives for now?
rationale: This adds config surface and changes the core execution authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent product/security contract or default behavior.

options.title: Design core confirmation gate
options.body: Proceed with a backward-compatible core gate that composes with existing exec and plugin approvals and defines deterministic approve, deny, timeout, transcript, and channel behavior.

options.title: Keep plugin and exec primitives only
options.body: Decline a built-in gate for now and direct operators to existing exec approval settings or plugin policies for tool-specific confirmations.

options.title: Fold into generic HITL interrupt work
options.body: Move the implementation under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/83276 while keeping this issue's same-response confirmation case as explicit acceptance criteria.

recommendation.title: Design core confirmation gate
recommendation.body: Proceed with a backward-compatible core gate that composes with existing exec and plugin approvals and defines deterministic approve, deny, timeout, transcript, and channel behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue timeline already routed this area to vincentkoc, and the remaining decision crosses hook/type/config surfaces where they have recent adjacent history.
